input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The condition uses all(...) where the docstring says the section is written if at least one argument is documented. This should be any(...).
- rationale: Trigger: a command with one documented and one undocumented argument. all() is False, so the whole "Positional arguments" section is omitted and the documented argument's help disappears. When there are no arguments, all([]) is True, so an empty "Positional arguments" section is emitted with write_dl([]).
critique: The finding identifies the same all() vs any() mistake in the guard. It describes both failure paths: mixed documented and undocumented arguments drop the section, and zero arguments produce an empty header.
